definitions.explanation: Having no defects or weaknesses whatsoever. A four-character idiom emphasizing total completeness and lack of any flaw.

examples.japanese: {完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}な⟦{人間|にんげん}→人間：03523_ningen⟧はいない。
⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ヒーロー→ヒーロー：11262_hiiroo⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{描|えが}かれている→描く：02013_egaku⟧。
examples.english: He is depicted as a flawless hero.

examples.japanese: {完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{求|もと}める→求める：02316_motomeru⟧あまり、⟦いつ→いつ：00536_itsu⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{作品|さくひん}→作品：02776_sakuhin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{完成|かんせい}させられない→完成させる：02519_kanseisaseru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Some people are so obsessed with perfection that they can never finish their work.

notes:
USAGE:
{完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ} is a ⟦{四字熟語|よじじゅくご}→四字熟語：15663_yojijukugo⟧ composed of ⟦{完全|かんぜん}→完全：01552_kanzen⟧ (complete, perfect) and ⟦{無欠|むけつ}→無欠：21825_muketsu⟧ (without defect). It is often used with ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ as a modifier ({完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧) or with な as a na-adjective.

In practice, it is frequently used in the negative — pointing out that nothing is truly {完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ} — or to describe idealized fictional characters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}な⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ (a perfect person)
- {完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧アリバイ (an airtight alibi)
- {完全無欠|かんぜんむけつ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{目指|めざ}す→目指す：10528_mezasu⟧ (aim for perfection)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{非|ひ}→非：28419_hi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{打|う}ちどころ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧ — "without any fault" (idiomatic)
- ⟦{完璧|かんぺき}→完璧：09505_kanpeki⟧ — "perfect, flawless" (more common in everyday speech)
